articles.title: Maharashtra gives taxi and tuk-tuk drivers a year to learn Marathi language
articles.summary: A new rule making it mandatory for drivers to learn Marathi or lose their licence had sparked protests.
articles.body:
An Indian state has given taxi and tuk-tuk drivers one more year to learn the local language after a new rule making it mandatory sparked protests.

Transport officials in the western state of Maharashtra had begun testing drivers' ability to conduct basic conversations in Marathi, the state's official language, on 20 August. Those who failed were given a month to learn the language, after which they risked having their licences suspended or cancelled.

The government said the requirement was meant to improve communication between drivers and passengers and ensure safer journeys.

But the rule alarmed drivers' unions, who argued that workers should not risk losing their livelihoods while they were still learning the language. Many of the drivers are migrants who came to Maharashtra from other parts of India in search of work, including the populous Hindi-speaking states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

Amid protests, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced last week that the drivers would be given another year to learn Marathi, as many had been out of the formal education system for years and needed more time.

State Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik has said that drivers will be expected to learn Marathi during the year and that there will be more extensions.

Maharashtra has almost 979,000 valid tuk-tuk and taxi permits, nearly half of them in the Mumbai metropolitan region.

The extension has brought some relief to drivers who had feared losing their ability to work.

"We were worried that if our licences were suspended, our daily income would be affected," says Lakhan Pandey, a taxi driver in Mumbai. "Now we feel somewhat relieved."

But the row has reopened a much older debate in Maharashtra, where questions of language, migration and jobs have shaped politics for decades.

"The issue is not simply about communication between drivers and passengers, but about Marathi identity, migration and employment," says Prakash Akolkar, a journalist, author and political analyst.

Those tensions stretch back to the creation of Maharashtra itself. The state was formed in 1960 after a long campaign for a Marathi-speaking state.

As Mumbai grew into India's financial centre, it drew generations of migrants from across the country in search of work. Language became increasingly entwined with arguments over jobs and opportunities for Marathi speakers.

In 1966, the Shiv Sena, a regional political party rooted in Marathi nationalism, was founded on a "sons of the soil" platform, arguing that Marathi speakers were losing jobs to migrants. It went on to become one of Maharashtra's most powerful political forces, with Marathi identity at the heart of its appeal.

Today, Maharashtra is governed by a coalition led by Fadnavis's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and one faction of the Shiv Sena, which split in 2022. The rival faction and another regional party, the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), have also championed the Marathi cause.

Akolkar says it is reasonable to expect people who move to a state to learn some of the local language. But he draws a distinction between that and the politics around it.

"Ordinary people do not always treat language with the same intensity as political parties," he says, adding that parties have often raised the issue when it suits the political circumstances.

Deepak Pawar, a political scientist and president of the Marathi Abhyas Kendra (Marathi Training Centre), which promotes the language, takes a stronger view. He argues that people who have lived in Maharashtra for years should already have acquired at least a basic knowledge of Marathi.

Refusing to learn the local language after living and working in the state for years is "linguistic arrogance", he says.

It's a tension that has played out in other states including Karnataka, where language activists fear their local language - Kannada - is being marginalised as many migrants believe they can get by using Hindi or English.

In Maharashtra, the government says drivers are not expected to read or write Marathi, or to speak it fluently. Under changes to the state's motor vehicle rules, they are required to have a "working knowledge" of the language.

To help them learn, the government has organised classes focused on Marathi words and phrases drivers might need at work - asking passengers where they want to go, discussing fares or giving directions.

Around 166,000 drivers have completed the training and passed an oral test, according to the state's transport department.

Munawar Sheikh, a 58-year-old tuk-tuk driver, was among those who signed up.

Over four days at a training centre in Thane, near Mumbai, he and other drivers learnt 16 commonly used questions and phrases, including "Where do you want to go?", "don't worry" and "the fare will be according to the meter".

At the end, they took an oral test, with those who passed receiving a certificate they could show transport officials during inspections.

Sheikh says the course taught him enough Marathi to manage basic conversations with passengers.

But for some drivers, finding the time to learn is part of the problem.

Ajay Singh, a taxi driver in Mumbai, says he wants to learn Marathi but has struggled to fit classes around his working day.

"From the time we wake up until late at night, we have to drive. Otherwise, there is no food on the table," he says. "Taking a few hours out of the day for a class is financially difficult for me."

Singh says he earns between 1,500 and 2,000 rupees ($17-$23; £13-£17) a day and worries that losing even a few days' income could leave him struggling to pay rent and his children's school fees.

Instead, he is trying to learn while he works - listening to Marathi radio stations while driving and practising with Marathi-speaking passengers.

Lakhan Pandey, also a driver, says the extra year has made a significant difference.

He says he never objected to learning Marathi - he just wanted enough time to do it.

"We live here, we work here. Of course we should learn Marathi," he says. "Just give us the time to learn it without putting our livelihoods at risk."

articles.title: The Grand Tour's new presenters: 'I hope we prove the critics wrong'
articles.summary: A new trio has taken the wheel of the motoring TV show from Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May.
articles.body:
For more than two decades, Top Gear and The Grand Tour were defined as much by the three men presenting them as by the cars they drove.

Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May built one of television's most recognisable partnerships, meaning anyone taking over The Grand Tour was always going to face a daunting task.

Now YouTubers James Engelsman and Thomas Holland and, perhaps most unexpectedly, train enthusiast-turned-internet star Francis Bourgeois are stepping into their shoes for the new series.

And, with initial reviews generally mixed, they knew they had some convincing to do.

"They literally changed the car world," Holland says of the previous trio.

He understands why some fans have questions about whether the show should continue with anyone else.

"They're completely justified to feel that, because they did the same thing that we did - which is grow up watching Clarkson, Hammond and May.

"The show was a very important part of our lives as car enthusiasts."

Engelsman says they themselves initially had many of the same doubts that viewers will have.

"We've had all the same reactions that the audience has had to every part of this process like, 'Who would do that? What an idiot.'

"We've been through it all and we're just lucky enough to have come out the other side and realised, 'OK, this is actually all stuff that could work.'"

"Now we've filmed it, I'm just excited to show the world," Bourgeois says. "We've done our absolute best and the critics will be critics and I hope that we will prove them wrong."

Holland adds that he hopes people will give the show a chance before judging.

"Have a watch and if you don't like it, you're well within your rights, I can't force anyone to like anything."

For a show built around the chemistry of its three former presenters, finding a replacement trio with such chemistry was always going to be as important as finding people who knew about cars.

Engelsman and Holland are an already established double act as the presenters of Throttle House, a motoring YouTube channel with more than three million subscribers.

The bigger unknown was who would become their third presenter.

That search eventually led the show's producers to Francis Bourgeois, a social media star better known for standing on railway platforms than behind the wheel of a supercar.

Engelsman says he and Holland had done chemistry testing with a number of people, but Bourgeois immediately felt different.

"As soon as Francis showed up, we were like: 'That guy'," Holland says.

Bourgeois remembers their first meeting taking place on a leather sofa in a hotel outside Basingstoke, where they mostly talked about what cars they owned.

By the time filming began, Holland says there was no need to consciously work out how to make the three-person dynamic function as "it just worked and clicked immediately".

While the chemistry came quickly, actually finding out they had the job was much less straightforward. Engelsman says there was "no immediate moment" when they were formally told they had been chosen.

"It was the most gradual thing," he says.

He and Holland initially thought they were simply part of a wider audition process, but then found themselves repeatedly being invited into writers' rooms and asked for their views on ideas for the show.

For Bourgeois, that uncertainty may have been helpful as he admits he'd "just fall apart and start crying" if he'd found out about the job.

There is a clear generational shift with the new presenters, all three of whom built their profiles on social media - and critics have been mixed on how successfully that translates to The Grand Tour.

The Independent's three-star review described the reboot as "all rather safe" and said the presenters feel "stilted".

The Guardian's review agreed and called the trio a "decent, if slightly anonymous, presence" who seem "quite meek and pleasant, and without any obvious dynamic".

But it did praise Bourgeois, with Stuart Heritage calling him "the most enthusiastic enthusiast currently working on planet Earth".

The FT also awarded the show three-stars and said that while the big budget spectacles are enjoyable to watch, they also feel "a little muted".

It added that "the real question is whether a series that has been driven by big personalities like Clarkson, May and Hammond can survive with a new team".

Bourgeois may be best known for his ecstatic trainspotting videos but he says his love of cars goes back just as far.

Growing up near Willesden Junction in London, there were plenty of trains to watch, but he was also fascinated by the cars outside his home.

"There was a particular Mitsubishi Legnum VR-4 that was outside my parents' flat window and I just loved it," he tells me. "I suppose with my social media, I'm just showing one of my passions and I have really wanted to let out that car enthusiasm too.

"It's nice that these two sides of my very strong passions are in harmony together and it's been a real pleasure to drive some of the cars on The Grand Tour."

His enthusiasm for transport more generally has already rubbed off on his co-presenters who say they've become "very educated by Francis on many things during long walks and long drives".

Bourgeois is even lobbying for The Grand Tour to devote an episode to another of his interests: power stations. And he has found a surprisingly receptive audience in Clarkson.

When the new trio met their predecessors, Bourgeois says seeing Clarkson in person gave him "a flutter in my tummy" and the pair bonded, inevitably, over trains, before moving on to power stations, and a lengthy discussion about cheeseburgers.

Engelsman says all three former presenters were supportive of their successors and "were very paternal and caring about it".

"They all seemed quite excited for there to be a new iteration," Engelsman says, adding that Clarkson even told them: "We'll look after you".

articles.title: Virgin's Richard Branson: Flight price rises due to 'foolish leaders' starting wars
articles.summary: Middle East tensions have choked the production and transportation of oil, causing a surge in the price of car and jet fuels.
articles.body:
Virgin Group founder Sir Richard Branson has blamed flight price rises on "foolish leaders" starting wars, in a thinly veiled reference to the US-Israel conflict with Iran.

Middle East tensions have choked the production and transportation of millions of barrels of oil, causing a surge in the price of car and jet fuels, which are made from oil.

In May, Virgin Atlantic added a fuel surcharge to ticket prices in response.

US President Donald Trump has repeatedly defended the conflict as necessary for peace and security long-term.

However, Sir Richard said there was "no need" for the war.

"The Iran conflict was completely unnecessary. There was a nuclear agreement between Iran and the rest of the world that had been negotiated by President Obama and a lot of European people.

"It was working, so there was no need to rip it up... And this war has just resulted in much higher oil prices all over the world. And inflation has been one of the consequences."

The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.

The European benchmark jet fuel price had been hovering around $800 (£590) a tonne but spiked following the outbreak of the Iran war, reaching a peak of over $1,800 in April. It has since dropped to around $1,450.

Virgin Atlantic's chief executive, Corneel Koster, told the BBC that for "this level of fuel price" fuel surcharges were "absolutely required", adding that it's "hard to be optimistic at this moment about the situation in the Middle East".

The surcharge Virgin introduced added £50 to an economy class fare, £180 to premium and £360 to business class.

Air fares soar by nearly 25% as Iran war forces flights to re-route

Airlines cut flights and hike fares as fuel prices surge

In April, analysis from consultancy firm Teneo found the Iran war had led to a 25% increase in air fares .

And this week Ryanair said it would reduce its winter schedule because of higher fuel prices and warned European short-haul fares would "increase materially" if jet fuel prices continue to rise until next summer.

Yet, despite the higher costs, Koster said Virgin did not plan to make any big changes to its winter schedule.

He said winter capacity had already been slightly reduced a few months ago and added that if there was low demand on certain routes "in the depths of winter", there would be some trimming or "capacity discipline", but not "big percentages".

The airline expects to fly 95% of its regular schedule.

Sir Richard was speaking to the BBC as Virgin Atlantic announced it had secured a contract to fly Team GB and ParalympicsGB to Los Angeles for the Summer Olympics in 2028.

The airline took the contract from rival British Airways, which had been doing it since the 2008 games in Beijing .

articles.title: Unruly passenger arrested after being restrained with duct tape during flight
articles.summary: The plane to Newark was diverted to Baltimore due to the disturbance.
articles.body:
A man was arrested for alleged unruly behavior on an American Airlines flight causing it to divert to Baltimore on Thursday night, according to the airline and investigators.

Arthur Lundeen, 67, of Arizona, was restrained to his seat with duct tape and his hands were restrained with zip ties, according to the Maryland Transportation Authority Police, which arrested him after the plane landed.

The incident took place on American Airlines flight AA 618, which took off from Dallas and was en route to Newark, according to the FBI and the airline.

Juan Mejia, a passenger on that flight and a former law enforcement officer, told ABC he began hearing a disturbance about three quarters of the way into the flight.

"[The] gentleman sitting two rows behind us started becoming belligerent, making derogatory remarks to the staff of American Airlines and other passengers, racial slurs, vulgar language, very offensive to the women" sitting in the row behind the man, Mejia said.

Mejia and his friend Richard Olenick, who were on board the flight, told ABC they were monitoring the situation and intervened after they claimed Lundeen became physical.

"Juan immediately knew that action had to be taken. He got up right away and jumped in the seat right next to the passenger and began working on restraining him in order to keep the situation contained," Olenick told ABC.

Authorities did not provide details of the disruption that took place during the flight, but the plane was diverted to Baltimore Washington International (BWI) Airport around 10:15 p.m., the Federal Aviation Administration, which is also probing the incident, said.

The two passengers said they stayed with Lundeen until law enforcement officials boarded the plane and took him into custody after they landed in Baltimore.

"We weren't looking to hurt this individual; we were looking more to restrain him and control him, so it didn't escalate to go any further," Mejia said.

Lundeen was removed from the plane and the flight continued to Newark, American Airlines said in a statement.

Lundeen was charged with disorderly conduct and second-degree assault "for incidents that occurred aboard the aircraft at BWI Airport," the MDTA Police said.

The reported incident that took place in the air is being investigated by the FBI.

"Lundeen was cleared by paramedics for an open wound on his arm that was noticed by officers while being taken into custody," the MTDA Police said in a statement.

"The safety ​and ​security ​of our customers ​and team members ​is our top ​priority and ​we ​do not ​tolerate violence," American Airlines said in a statement.

The FBI said the investigation is ongoing.

ABC News' Jack Date contributed to this report.

articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump on Friday issued a fresh threat to Iran, saying that the America could \"hit\" its  heavily fortified underground nuclear site.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Friday issued a fresh threat to Iran, saying that the America could "hit" its heavily fortified underground nuclear site "very soon."Speaking to reporters at the Oval Office, Trump warned that Pickaxe Mountain could be targeted if the US detects activity there."We may hit Pickaxe very soon because if there was anything going on with Pickaxe," Trump said, adding that US intelligence was closely monitoring activity at the site."We know everybody that's moving at Pickaxe; we know everybody that's moving everywhere all over Iran. And if anything goes bad, we hit them; we hit them hard," Trump said.He also defended Unites States' military campaign in Iran and said that its primary objective was to prevent Tehran from acquiring nuclear weapon."We're in five months now. And you know what we did in five months? They're not going to have a nuclear weapon; that's what we did," Trump said."Iran will not have a nuclear weapon because if they did, you probably wouldn't be standing here very long," he added.Pickaxe Mountain is located near Iran’s heavily damaged Natanz uranium-enrichment facility and is described as a heavily fortified underground complex comprising two deeply buried tunnel systems.The Wall Street Journal had earlier reported that Israeli intelligence believes Iran has moved thousands of centrifuges to the deeply buried site.The facility’s underground construction is believed to make it significantly more resistant to conventional aerial strikes. Any potential US decision to target the site could therefore mark a major escalation in the campaign against Iran’s nuclear infrastructure.Asked about his deputy JD Vance's assertion that months of on-and-off attacks in the Middle East are not a war, Trump said that conflict in Iran is “small potatoes”“I can understand what he’s saying,” Trump said.“I call it a military conflict because it’s small potatoes for us. It's not a big thing," he added.His remarks came days after US Central Command said American forces had completed a fresh wave of strikes against Iranian military targets.According to CENTCOM, the operations targeted facilities linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, including air-defence installations, radar systems, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites.CENTCOM said the strikes followed what it described as recent “attempted attacks” by the IRGC on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and US service members.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Pizza, meth & guns: Indian national illegally living in US charged with drug trafficking
articles.summary: US News: An Indian national unlawfully living in the United States has been charged with allegedly distributing methamphetamine from a pizza outlet in Californ.
articles.body: An Indian national unlawfully living in the United States has been charged with allegedly distributing methamphetamine from a pizza outlet in California, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) said.He has also been charged with possessing firearms in connection with drug trafficking.According to court documents, 50-year-old Kawal Preet Singh sold wholesale quantities of methamphetamine from a Round Table Pizza restaurant he operated in Dinuba, California, while armed with illegal firearms.A federal grand jury returned an indictment against Singh, charging him with “distribution of methamphetamine, possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime”, US attorney Eric Grant announced, according to the DOJ.The charges follow a federal investigation into organised Indian crime in California’s Central Valley, which identified Singh as a subject, the DOJ said.On August 18, federal agents searched Singh’s home and business and seized more than 40 pounds of methamphetamine, three firearms and more than $10,000 in cash, according to the department.The DOJ said Singh faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years and a maximum of life in prison, along with a fine of up to $10 million, if convicted on the drug-trafficking charges.He also faces a mandatory minimum of five years in prison, to be served consecutively to any other sentence, and up to life imprisonment for possessing a firearm in furtherance of drug trafficking.The department stressed that “The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.”The Federal Bureau of Investigation and Homeland Security Investigations conducted the investigation.The case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force initiative, described by the DOJ as a “whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organisations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: New York City shooting: Man fatally shot on Brooklyn Bridge after 'ignoring orders to drop weapon'
articles.summary: US News: A knife-wielding man walking on the cables of New York City’s iconic Brooklyn Bridge was fatally shot after he allegedly ignored police orders to drop.
articles.body: A knife-wielding man walking on the cables of New York City’s iconic Brooklyn Bridge was fatally shot after he allegedly ignored police orders to drop the weapon, authorities said on Friday (local time).Also Read | Times Square stabbing: 1 killed, another critically injured; suspect shot dead by NYPDThe man, whose name has not yet been released, was shot after moving within feet of an officer who was trying to help him climb down.According to Gerard Dowling, commanding officer of the New York City Police Department’s Emergency Services Unit, the man told the police rescue team to kill him and claimed he had a bomb.“The officers spoke to him for about an hour... they wanted to help him and bring him down and told him to drop the knife multiple times. The officers began to move backwards away from the male when he began to climb down, but were not able to move as quickly as the subject, who was approaching them,” Dowling told a news conference later.He added that the man came within three feet of an officer and raised his arm, with the knife extended toward the officer. At that point, another officer shot him once. The rescue team then brought the man down, and he later died at a hospital.Police body cameras recorded the encounter. In addition to the knife, a flashlight was recovered.When a reporter asked whether police had found a bomb, Dowling replied that was part of the ongoing investigation.New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani posted online that officers responded after receiving a 911 call about a man “who appeared to be attempting to jump from the bridge.”“As is standard when an NYPD officer discharges a firearm, the department will conduct an internal investigation, and body-worn camera footage will be released,” Mamdani said.The Brooklyn Bridge, which opened in 1883, is a cable-supported suspension bridge connecting Manhattan and Brooklyn.Its towers rise 276.5 feet (84 metres) above the water. It was not immediately clear how high above the water the man and the police officers were when the incident occurred.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Happy Teachers' Day 2026: Best 30+ wishes and messages for teachers, colleagues, bosses, students, and friends
articles.summary: Trending News: Some teachers stay in your memory for years. Not necessarily because of the subject they taught, but because of the way they made you feel.You remembe.
articles.body: Some teachers stay in your memory for years. Not necessarily because of the subject they taught, but because of the way they made you feel.You remember the teacher who gave you extra time when you were struggling. The one who noticed when you were unusually quiet. The colleague who showed you the ropes without making you feel like you were asking silly questions. Even a friend can end up teaching you a thing or two about life.That is what makes Teachers' Day special. It is not only about classrooms and textbooks. It is about people who, in one way or another, helped us learn.If you are sending a message this year, you don't have to make it sound like a greeting card. A few honest words usually work better. Here are some wishes for different people in your life.Happy Teachers' Day wishes for teachers1. Happy Teachers' Day! Thank you for making even the difficult lessons feel a little easier.2. I may not remember every lesson from school, but I remember the teachers who made a difference. Thank you for being one of them.3. Happy Teachers' Day to someone who taught with patience, encouraged us to keep trying and never made a wrong answer feel like the end of the world.4. Thank you for believing in me on the days when I wasn't very sure of myself. Happy Teachers' Day!5. A good teacher gives you knowledge. A memorable teacher makes you want to learn more. Thank you for doing both.6. Happy Teachers' Day! Looking back, I realise some of your simplest advice stayed with me the longest.7. Thank you for all the explanations, encouragement and second chances. They mattered more than you probably knew.8. Wishing you a very Happy Teachers' Day. Some of the things you taught us still come back to us when we need them most.9. Thank you for inspiring us, guiding us, and helping us become better every day.10. Wishing you a very Happy Teachers’ Day! Your wisdom and kindness have made a lasting difference in our lives11. Thank you for being a wonderful teacher and a constant source of motivation. Happy Teachers’ Day 2026!12. Your lessons go far beyond books and classrooms. Thank you for teaching us the values that truly matter. Happy Teachers’ Day!13. Wishing a very Happy Teachers’ Day to the teacher who made learning meaningful, exciting, and unforgettable.Happy Teachers’ Day messages for colleaguesLet's be honest, every workplace has that one person everyone goes to with a “Can you quickly show me how to do this?”9. Happy Teachers' Day to the colleague who somehow always knows what to do when the rest of us are figuring it out!10. Thank you for sharing what you know without ever making anyone feel uncomfortable for asking. Happy Teachers' Day!11. Some of my best work lessons didn't come from training sessions. They came from watching and learning from people like you.12. Happy Teachers' Day! Here's to the colleague who has answered my “one small question” approximately a hundred times.13. Work is much easier when people are willing to help each other grow. Thank you for always being that person.14. Happy Teachers' Day to a colleague I've learnt far more from than you probably realise.Happy Teachers Day wishes for your bossA boss can give instructions. A good leader also leaves you with something to learn.15. Happy Teachers' Day! Thank you for the feedback that made me better, even when I didn't particularly enjoy hearing it.16. Thank you for trusting me with opportunities that pushed me to learn and improve. Wishing you a very Happy Teachers' Day.17. Some of the best professional lessons come from watching how someone handles pressure, people and problems. Thank you for being a great example.18. Happy Teachers' Day to a boss who understands that making mistakes is sometimes part of getting better.19. Thank you for the guidance, the honest conversations and the encouragement along the way. It has made a difference.20. Wishing you a Happy Teachers' Day. I am grateful for the things I have learnt under your guidance.Happy Teachers’ Day messages for studentsTeachers learn from students too. Ask anyone who has spent enough time in a classroom.21. Happy Teachers' Day to my students! Your questions often make me look at familiar things in a completely different way.22. Never stop asking questions. Even the ones that seem obvious can lead to the most interesting conversations.23. Happy Teachers' Day! Don't be afraid of getting things wrong. Nobody learns much by being right all the time.24. Thank you for bringing your curiosity, ideas and energy into the classroom. You make teaching worthwhile.25. You may think I am the one teaching you, but believe me, I learn plenty from you too. Happy Teachers' Day!26. Keep asking, keep trying and keep being curious. Those qualities will take you much further than a perfect answer ever will.Happy Teachers' Day wishes for friendsSome friends are basically teachers without the formal title.27. Happy Teachers' Day to the friend who has given me advice I didn't ask for and, annoyingly, was usually right.28. Somewhere between all our conversations, you've taught me quite a few things about life. Thank you!29. Happy Teachers' Day to my unofficial life coach, reality checker and occasional lecturer.30. We've learnt a lot together, from school days to figuring out adulthood. Here's to the lessons still to come.31. Thank you for the conversations that made me think, the advice that helped and the honesty I sometimes didn't want but needed.32. Happy Teachers' Day to a friend who has taught me that sometimes the best lesson is simply to take things one day at a time.Short Teachers' Day messages for WhatsApp and social media33. Happy Teachers' Day to everyone who has taught me something worth carrying forward.34. Some lessons fade. The people who taught them don't. Happy Teachers' Day!35. Thank you to every teacher, mentor, colleague, friend and student who has taught me something along the way.36. Happy Teachers' Day! Grateful for the lessons that came from classrooms and the ones that came from life.37. To everyone who ever helped me learn, grow or try again, thank you. Happy Teachers Day!38. Happy Teachers' Day! Here's to the people who made learning a little easier and life a little wiser.Why do we celebrate Teachers' Day on September 5?September 5 is observed as Teachers' Day to mark the birth anniversary of Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, a philosopher, academic and former President.The occasion is a reminder to appreciate the people who play a part in our education and growth. And while the traditional image of a teacher is someone standing in front of a classroom, life has a way of giving us teachers in unexpected places.A colleague can teach you confidence. A friend can teach you when to walk away. A boss can teach you how to handle pressure. A student can remind you to stay curious.So, if there is someone who taught you something you still remember, this might be a good day to tell them.No elaborate speech required.Just a simple thank you can do the job.Thumb image: Canva Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Bangladesh measles outbreak nears 1,000 child deaths as cases cross 180,000
articles.summary: South Asia News: Bangladesh’s worst measles outbreak in decades has killed close to 1,000 children with suspected and confirmed cases now surpassing 180,000, according.
articles.body: Bangladesh’s worst measles outbreak in decades has killed close to 1,000 children with suspected and confirmed cases now surpassing 180,000, according to the latest health ministry figures.More than 1,000 suspected cases are being reported each day as hospitals struggle to treat a growing number of severely ill children, news agency AFP reported.At Dhaka’s Shishu Hospital, 101 children are currently admitted with suspected or confirmed measles. According to the health ministry, at least 986 children have died since March.“Just an hour ago, a child died, and they wheeled him out in front of us,” 30-year-old Rima Akter told AFP on Thursday. “We saw two children die today.”Akter’s nine-month-old son, Sabit Haque, is among the children being treated at the hospital.Measles is highly contagious and spreads through coughs and sneezes. Two doses of vaccine can largely prevent the disease, but once infected, there is no specific treatment. Young children, particularly those who are malnourished, face a higher risk of severe complications.The impact is evident in the hospital’s wards. Doctors said many children are arriving at hospitals with severe respiratory problems and infections, while malnutrition is further reducing their ability to fight the disease.The outbreak has exposed gaps in Bangladesh’s immunisation programme. A measles vaccination campaign planned for 2024 was delayed by the uprising that toppled former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, while strikes and political instability disrupted a planned 2025 campaign.SM Ziauddin Hyder, special assistant to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for health, described the outbreak as “devastating”.“There was a gap of a significant number of children missing the doses,” Hyder said. “Healthcare workers... are vaccinating these children to close the gap.”Bangladesh has since launched a mass vaccination drive, but the continued rise in infections has placed renewed pressure on health authorities to close immunisation gaps and strengthen hospital capacity.One infant dies of measles in USIn a separate development, one infant in Pennsylvania has died from measles amid a growing outbreak in the US, with Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr confirming the death on Friday, citing information from a county coroner.Vaccination rates in the US have declined, with medical groups citing rising vaccine hesitancy as a key factor. Pennsylvania has reported 540 measles cases this year, according to Reuters. The state health department also notified the CDC of two measles-associated deaths on August 25 before publishing the deaths on its website.The World Health Organization has previously stressed that measles vaccination is highly effective and that sustained high coverage is critical to preventing outbreaksCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Bengaluru woman 'abducted, assaulted, stripped' over loan dispute
articles.summary: BENGALURU: A dispute over loans and mounting interest allegedly took a horrifying turn after a woman accused four people of abducting her and her youn.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A dispute over loans and mounting interest allegedly took a horrifying turn after a woman accused four people of abducting her and her young son, confining them, assaulting her and threatening to circulate a video of her after allegedly forcing her to strip.Fathima (name changed), who works as a domestic help, had borrowed Rs 50,000 from accused Nazath Begum, agreeing to repay it in weekly instalments of Rs 5,000.She had also borrowed Rs 1 lakh from Reshma Banu around two years ago and was paying monthly interest. Due to financial difficulties, she claimed she had fallen behind on both payments.Fathima accused Reshma of repeatedly demanding the pending interest and visiting her house, prompting her to block Reshma’s phone numbers. She further claimed that the threats continued through Reshma’s mother, forcing her to stay away from home for nearly two months.On August 27, Nazath called her, claiming she had some work for her and would pay her for it. Fathima went to her house in Metro Layout with her younger son at around 5.30 pm.While she was feeding her son, Nazath stepped outside and spoke to someone. Soon after, Reshma, her husband Suhail and two others entered the house and locked the door.Fathima told police that Suhail demanded Rs 11 lakh, including interest, and hit her hand with a knife. When her son began crying, she claimed Reshma and Suhail assaulted her and snatched her mobile phone.Around 7 pm, she and her son were forced into an auto and taken to a house near Kumbalagodu.At Reshma’s house, both Nazath and Suhail told her to work as a prostitute if she could not repay the money and threatened to bring other men.She and her son were kept locked inside a room overnight. The following day, she developed a fever but was again assaulted by Nazath, Suhail and Saif.In the evening, Fathima claimed Nazath forced her to remove her clothes and recorded a video, threatening to make it viral if she failed to repay the money.The next day, Reshma, Suhail and Nazath took her to a lawyer near a market and made her sign certain papers before returning her to the Kumbalagodu house.The woman eventually managed to alert her family when she was allowed to step out to use the toilet. Her family complained to the police, who rushed to the house and rescued her.Chandra Layout police have arrested Nazath, Reshma and Suhail and are investigating the case. articles.title: China landslide: More than 10 buried in Jiangxi days after Typhoon Saudel triggers torrential rain, floods
articles.summary: China News: A landslide struck Gaoping town in China’s Jiangxi province, burying more than 10 people, state broadcaster CCTV reported. The incident comes as China.
articles.body: A landslide struck Gaoping town in China’s Jiangxi province, burying more than 10 people, state broadcaster CCTV reported. The incident comes as China grapples with severe weather, with Typhoon Saudel bringing torrential rain and flooding to coastal areas.Rescue operations were launched after the landslide in Gaoping, with authorities working to locate the people reported trapped. Further details on the condition of those trapped were not immediately available.Typhoon Saudel-triggered floods inundated homes and swept through tea-growing communities in Fujian and Guangdong on Friday. Firefighters waded through waist-deep waters in Fuding to rescue elderly residents, while flooding in Jinxi village brought down a three-storey house. Authorities also closed schools, shut tourist attractions and suspended 24 ferry routes as torrential rain heightened the risk of flash floods and landslides.The latest incident follows the devastating flash floods and mudslides that struck parts of Nepal and Tibet on August 26, leaving a high death toll and dozens still missing. Nepal Police said on Saturday that the death toll had risen to 1,344 as rescue and relief operations continued. The police shared the latest toll in a post on X, while authorities have been dealing with the wider aftermath of the disaster, including concerns over contaminated drinking water and the possible spread of communicable diseases in affected areas.In neighbouring Tibet, the death toll from floods and a mudslide that hit a border crossing between China and Nepal rose to 31, state-run news agency Xinhua reported on Friday. Xinhua said 531 people remained missing following the disaster on the Tibet side.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
